title: Labor on the Douro River
creator: Manoel de Oliveira
description: Douro, Faina Fluvial: Manoel de Oliveira’s first film, a silent short about the dockworkers, boatmen, and fishwives of the Douro waterfront. Oliveira, born in Porto in 1908, kept making films until he died in 2015 at 106.

title: Aniki-Bóbó
creator: Manoel de Oliveira
description: Oliveira’s first feature, about a gang of children playing in the riverside streets below the Luís I bridge, acted by local children rather than actors. It is often seen as a forerunner of Italian neorealism.

title: Porto of My Childhood
creator: Manoel de Oliveira
description: Porto da Minha Infância: Oliveira, then in his 90s, returns to the city of his youth in the 1910s and 1920s, mixing memories, reenactments, and archive film of cafés, theaters, and streets that have since disappeared.

title: Visit, or Memories and Confessions
creator: Manoel de Oliveira
place: House of Cinema Manoel de Oliveira, Serralves
description: Visita ou Memórias e Confissões: Oliveira filmed this tour of his family home in Porto in 1982, as debts forced him to sell it, and asked that it be shown only after his death. It premiered in 2015. His archive is now kept at Serralves.

title: Porto
creator: Gabe Klinger
description: A brief romance between an American drifter and a French student, played by Anton Yelchin and Lucie Lucas, told from three points of view over one night and its aftermath in Porto. Jim Jarmusch was an executive producer.
